cross_file_coherence.reason: All six files belong to the same DfT STATS19 Road Safety Open Data release for the 2024 data year. The three CSV tables (collision, vehicle, casualty) are linked by collision_index as confirmed by the data guide (seg_0162a94b5f71567ecadb0ba8: 'collision_index combines collision_year and collision_ref_no to form a unique ID. It can be used to join to Vehicle and Casualty'). The XLSX data guide defines fields and codes used across all three CSVs (e.g., junction_detail codes appear in the collision CSV header and are defined in the code list; vehicle_manoeuvre codes appear in the vehicle CSV and are defined in the code list). The DOCX severity-adjustment guidance documents methodology for adjustment fields present in the collision CSV (collision_adjusted_severity_serious, collision_adjusted_severity_slight, collision_injury_based, enhanced_severity_collision) and casualty CSV (casualty_adjusted_severity_serious, casualty_adjusted_severity_slight, casualty_injury_based, enhanced_casualty_severity). The PDF reviews the STATS19 collection system that produces all these files. collision_year=2024 is consistent across all sampled rows in all three CSVs. The XLSX is labeled '2024_code_list' and references '2024 STATS19 specification'. The DOCX covers 2004-latest year adjustment data. The PDF (2018 review, published March 2020) predates the 2024 data but covers the same STATS19 system; the 2024 data uses both 2011 and 2024 specifications as documented in the code list's historic vs new field distinctions.
